title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 — Jamaica count progression and media-specific accounting
purpose: Resolve as far as possible the long-standing 106/116 Jamaica count problem by restoring chronology, actor and counted output. A newly isolated early-March forecast of approximately 100 species shows that 106 is part of a plausible productivity sequence, while the institutional 116 remains a differently worded coloured-drawing total rather than a simple correction.

count_sequence.counted_object: collection/species expected from plants then blooming and Rudolf's productivity in examining them
count_sequence.source_wording_summary: Rudolf reckons from the plants blooming in March and his productivity in examining them that, if all goes well, he will be able to bring together a collection of approximately 100 species.
count_sequence.interpretation: prospective yield forecast based on phenology and work rate

count_sequence.counted_object: species with which Rudolf says he has finished his work
count_sequence.source_wording_summary: Before leaving Jamaica Rudolf tells his parents he has finished his work with 106 species.
count_sequence.interpretation: retrospective self-count of completed Jamaica work at departure

count_sequence.source: Foreign Students in the Gardens, Bulletin of the Botanical Department, Jamaica, p.18
count_sequence.counted_object: species represented in accurate coloured drawings by Blaschka
count_sequence.associated_output: Robert Cameron made dried collections of the same and other plants for the herbarium.
count_sequence.status: direct institutional report as preserved in project source register; exact page image remains desirable
count_sequence.interpretation: institutional pictorial-output count with a separately broader dried-collection statement

resolution.100_to_106: best read as forecast-to-completed progression. The approximately-100 early estimate is explicitly conditional on March flowering and Rudolf's productivity; the 106 departure count slightly exceeds that forecast.
resolution.106_to_116: remains unresolved and should not be forced into one corrected total. The nouns and actors differ: Rudolf counts species with which he has finished his work; the Jamaican report counts species in accurate coloured drawings. The institutional report also gives Cameron a dried collection of the same and other plants, creating a third, potentially broader material ledger.
resolution.digit_error_assessment: The early approximately-100 forecast makes Rudolf's later 106 internally plausible and reduces the likelihood that 106 is merely an OCR/transcription slip for 116. Image-level verification remains required for publication quotation.
resolution.preferred_status_label: media/accounting discrepancy, not simple numerical contradiction

jamaica_ledgers.unit: same and other plants; no single numeric total given in current report summary
separately enumerated or partially unidentified packets; not part of 106/116 by default
jamaica_ledgers.basis: Rudolf's letters sending seeds and discussing later cultivation

strongest_claim: Jamaica did not generate one master total. It generated multiple accounting surfaces tied to different media and decisions: a phenology/productivity forecast, Rudolf's completed-work self-count, an institutional coloured-drawing total, Cameron's dried collection, and separate propagule packets. The 106/116 gap is therefore evidence for media-specific bookkeeping until a source explicitly proves that both numbers were intended to count the same objects.
article_consequence: The Jamaica count problem can now function as a compact demonstration of the paper's broader method. Instead of normalizing discrepant totals, reconstruct the operation that produced each number. This turns numerical mismatch into evidence for how botanical encounters were converted into drawings, specimens and future cultivation.

figure_candidate.title: One field season, several ledgers
figure_candidate.visual_rule: Use separate lanes by medium/actor rather than a single rising total.
